pages.text: For forty days after Easter, Jesus showed His friends He was alive. He told them, "Wait in Jerusalem. The Holy Spirit will come and give you power."
On a mountain, Jesus said, "Go and teach all people. Baptize them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. I am with you always." Then He went up into heaven.
Two angels said, "Why do you stand looking at the sky? Jesus will come back." The friends went back to Jerusalem and prayed together.

thinkAboutIt.title: Think about it
thinkAboutIt.text: Jesus said, "I am with you always." We are baptized in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

pages.text: The apostles and Mary waited in Jerusalem and prayed together. Fifty days after Easter, they were all in one room.
Suddenly there was a sound like a strong wind. Tongues of fire rested on each of them, and the Holy Spirit filled them with courage and joy.
The friends went outside and told everyone about Jesus. People from many countries heard them in their own languages and were amazed!
That day, three thousand people were baptized. This was the birthday of the Church! The Holy Spirit still helps us today.

thinkAboutIt.title: Think about it
thinkAboutIt.text: At Pentecost, the Holy Spirit came, and the Church began. The Holy Spirit helps us be brave and love others.

pages.text: Saul did not believe in Jesus. He wanted to stop Jesus' followers. He set off for the city of Damascus to find them.
On the road, a bright light flashed from the sky, and Saul fell to the ground. A voice said, "Saul, why are you hurting me?" Saul asked, "Who are You?" "I am Jesus."
Saul could not see. His friends led him into Damascus. For three days he did not eat or drink, but he prayed.
A follower named Ananias prayed for Saul. Saul could see again, and he was baptized. He took the name Paul and told everyone about Jesus.

thinkAboutIt.title: Think about it
thinkAboutIt.text: Jesus changed Saul's heart, and Paul became a great missionary. Jesus can change hearts, too.

pages.text: The first followers of Jesus met often to pray, to listen to the apostles and to share bread together, the way Jesus had asked.
They shared everything they had. If someone needed food, others sold what they owned and gave to the poor, so no one went without.
They were glad and thanked God, and more and more people joined them. We are the same Church today, sharing and praying together.

thinkAboutIt.title: Think about it
thinkAboutIt.text: The first Christians prayed, shared and cared for each other. We do the same in the Church today.
